reason: The ceramic needs to become clean root medium, so the wash bench is the most direct place to start.
expectation: The blocks will be processed and washed into a usable growing medium.

effect: The ceramic is now washed, checked growing medium, ready for the beds.
reaction: The explanation of drainage and air spaces made the processing satisfying.
reason: The clean medium belongs in the empty growing beds.
expectation: The beds will be filled with porous medium.

reaction: The dry beds make the next step clear.
reason: The drinking water supply is the available clean water for the unwatered beds.
expectation: Clean water will fill the shared loop and wet the growing medium.

reaction: Seeing the water circulate through all three zones was a satisfying finish.

mostWorthwhile.text: Processing the ceramic was most worthwhile: breaking and washing it, then checking for leaching, connected the action to drainage and root aeration.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the beds was straightforward and predictable, though it was useful progress rather than a confusing step.

surprise.text: The leach check changed my understanding: clean-looking ceramic also needed to be checked for what it might release into the water.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each visibly prepared or watered the root medium.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the beds become a working food supply; the concise physical explanations made the construction interesting.
